title: Five Tests. Five Draws. India and England Have Shared the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy Without a Single Result.
excerpt: The 2026 series in England produced centuries from Jadeja, Sundar, Gill, and Pant, remarkable rearguard actions, and rain — but not a single winner across five matches.
body:
It is over. Five Tests across five of England's most storied grounds — Lord's, Headingley, Edgbaston, Old Trafford, and The Oval — and not a single match produced a winner.

India and England have shared the **Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy** after the 2026 series ended **0-0**, with all five Tests drawn. It is the first time since 1959 that an entire five-match Test series between two major nations has ended without a result in any match.

## A Series of Heroic Draws

The statistics will show five draws, but they will not capture how close each match came to producing a result.

At **Old Trafford** in the fourth Test, India's position looked dire before **Ravindra Jadeja** and **Washington Sundar** produced centuries that pulled the match back from the brink. Jadeja's innings — fighting, stubborn, and increasingly aggressive — was widely regarded as one of the finest rearguard knocks in recent Indian Test history.

**Shubman Gill** and **KL Rahul** were India's most consistent performers across the series. Gill, captaining the Test side, showed maturity beyond his years in negotiating English conditions. Rahul's counter-attacking instincts, particularly in the fourth and fifth Tests, repeatedly pulled India back from dangerous positions.

**Rishabh Pant** produced at least one innings of characteristic audacity per match, though his dismissals often came at moments when India needed consolidation rather than acceleration.

## England's Frustration

For England, the series represented a familiar frustration: dominance in sessions, control of conditions, and an inability to land the finishing blow. Their pace attack — led by the inexhaustible **Mark Wood** and an increasingly reliable new-ball partnership — consistently had India in trouble in the first sessions. But India's depth in batting, bolstered by contributions from the lower middle order, meant England could never quite force the endgame.

**Joe Root** continued his remarkable run of consistency, though a three-figure score eluded him until late in the series. The Edgbaston and Headingley Tests both saw England declare with what looked like winning leads, only for Indian resistance to hold firm.

## What It Means for India

For Indian fans — including the tens of thousands who traveled from across the UK and Europe to fill grounds at Lord's, Edgbaston, and Old Trafford — the series will feel like a missed opportunity. India had positions to push for victory in at least two of the five Tests but could not capitalize.

The pattern has persisted: India produce individual performances of brilliance abroad but cannot string together the sustained excellence needed to win multiple sessions in succession. Jadeja's century at Old Trafford was magnificent; it was also a rescue act, not a match-winning one.

For NRI cricket fans in the UK, though, the series delivered in atmosphere. The Bharat Army's presence at every ground was unmistakable, and the sight of Indian flags across the stands at The Oval for the fifth Test was a reminder of how deeply diaspora fans have embedded themselves in English cricket culture. Ticket demand for India matches now outstrips Ashes fixtures at most English grounds.

## The Trophy Is Shared

The Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy, inaugurated in 2025 when the previous series ended 2-2 in India, remains without a sole winner. The trophy — named after James Anderson and Sachin Tendulkar, two of the format's greatest practitioners — was designed to honor the rich history of the rivalry. But a 0-0 series is not the history either board envisioned.

India's next Test assignment is an away series against Afghanistan, starting later this week. Gill will captain the Test side, while Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma return for the ODI leg. The England experience — bruising, instructive, and ultimately inconclusive — will travel with them.

*The next India-England Test series is scheduled for 2029 in India, as part of the 2027-29 World Test Championship cycle.*
author: Diaspora Desk
